newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, mining shares in focus.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, mining shares in focus.

text.p: Stocks closed firmer on Tuesday on the back of falling interest rates, but brokers said a consolidation was likely on Wednesday as the index had climbed for six consecutive trading days.
Shares of mining companies remained on centre stage after news that a mining region would be developed as a resort.
The composite index ended 3.64 points higher at 713.43.

"Interest rates are falling as a result of the central bank's relaxed money supply. That helps buoy sentiment," said Lee Kil-ku of Hyundai Securities. The yields for three-year corporates fell to 11.90 percent from 11.93 percent on Monday.
Coal miner Dong Won Co Ltd rose 3,800 won to its daily limit of 52,400, and Daesung Resources Co Ltd, up 7,700 won to 107,000.
Young Poong Mining and Construction Co Ltd, a gold miner, went up 3,200 won to 47,300.

The Ministry of Construction and Transportation said a total of 2.54 trillion won would be invested by 2005 to develop a coal mining region in Kangwon Province into a leisure town, including ski trails, hotels and golf courses.
Samsung Electronics rose 800 won to 54,700 on expectations of price recovery, brokers said.
Volume was a healthy 41.37 million shares, compared with 29.31 million on Monday.
Gainers outpaced losers 522 to 283 with 106 unchanged.
Brokers said profit taking would emerge at around 720.
"Technically, the 720 level will pose a crossroads. It is hard to predict whether the level will be broken, but consolidation is likely," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The March futures contracts fell 0.3 of a point to 73.30, while the KOSPI 200 index gained 0.27 of a point to 74.64.
